meta.status_vocab: proved | measured-and-rechecked (CLAIMS level A or B, or re-derived here) | measured | unchecked | retired

bulk_density.label: Chaos fills 41.6% of cells
bulk_density.line: In the chaotic sea about 42 of every 100 faces are alive, whatever the size of the space.

symmetric_density.label: Symmetric chaos runs thinner
symmetric_density.line: Patterns with full cube symmetry are sparser: faces on mirror planes are alive only about 31% of the time.
symmetric_density.src: research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 phase agent, "Confined chaos: the 0.39 is a symmetry artefact"; STATUS storyline 3; CLAIMS P7
symmetric_density.claims: P7 A (phase agent and lead occupancy run agree); CLAIMS gives mirror planes as ~0.31-0.35

correlation_length.label: Neighbours barely know each other
correlation_length.line: Knowing one face tells you almost nothing about faces more than a cube away; patterns look the same in every direction.

damage_spreading.label: One flip spreads as a sphere
damage_spreading.line: Change one face and the difference grows into a ball moving at about 0.85 cubes per step.
damage_spreading.src: research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 phase agent, "Chaos proper"; CLAIMS P5

front_speeds.label: Chaos invades emptiness unevenly
front_speeds.line: Chaos eats into empty space at 0.18 cubes per step flat-on, 0.17 edge-on, and never across diagonal planes.
front_speeds.src: research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 phase agent, "Chaos proper"; STATUS storyline 1; CLAIMS P6
front_speeds.claims: P6 C; {111} = 0 is proved (T2), grade A

mean_field.label: Averages alone predict a wobble
mean_field.line: Ignoring correlations, the density would never settle but cycle through four values; real chaos is steady.

value.fix: neighbour-count overdispersion (intra-neighbourhood correlation 0.035-0.04) moves the fixed point to 0.416-0.42 and makes it stable

mean_field.claims: P3 A (auditor own calculation); the stabilising correction is measured

overcrowded_share.label: Two in five are overcrowded
overcrowded_share.line: At any moment 40% of faces have six or more live neighbours, the only thing keeping chaos going.
overcrowded_share.src: research/theory/threshold.md section 5 (table); research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-13 "where the chaos comes from"

immortal_torus.label: Big enough means never dies
immortal_torus.line: A space with no edges and more than about 600 faces keeps its chaos beyond a million steps.

value.N>=6 (648+ cells): none of 512 soups ended within 1e6 gens

immortal_torus.src: research/STATUS.md storyline 4; CLAIMS P8; research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 phase agent "Torus lifetimes"
immortal_torus.claims: P8 A+B (N=4: 1194 +- 53; N=5: 8.6e5 and 1.3e6 in two batches)

rule_survey.label: Gump among 960 rules
rule_survey.line: Many rules boil on a torus, but few keep chaos alive inside a closed box; gump sits at the edge.
rule_survey.src: research/phase/rules.csv (from survey.py + rulemap.py); figure research/figures/phase_rulemap.png; research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 phase agent "Rule space"
rule_survey.order_note: rows and columns in the order of phase_rulemap.png (rulemap.py sorts)

torus_class_codes.c: chaos: some whole-torus soup still running with >=10% of cells changing per gen at 3000 gens
torus_class_codes.s: slow: running, but <10% change per gen

rule_survey.torus_class_method: best outcome over four whole-torus soups, 24^3 cubes, p0 = 0.15/0.3/0.5/0.7, 3000 gens
rule_survey.log10_med_lifetime_method: log10 of median confined lifetime (cycle_start) of 16 soups, p = 0.35, octahedral vessel L1 radius 10 (doubled units); cap 1e5 gens (value 5.0 = at cap); values <1 clipped to 0
rule_survey.capped_note: digit = floor(runs of 16 that reached the 1e5 cap / 2), capped at 9

counts.gump_rank: longer-lived than 831 rules (832 counting ties with itself); 128 rules longer

one_count_removed.label: Remove any count: chaos collapses
one_count_removed.line: Take away any single birth or survival number and confined chaos dies about 100 times sooner.

add_S2_or_S7.label: Add survival 2 or 7: longer
add_S2_or_S7.line: Letting faces survive with two or with seven neighbours makes confined chaos outlast the survey entirely.

B45_S3457.label: Super-gump: 100x per step
B45_S3457.line: One extra survival number gives chaos that lasts about a hundred times longer each time the box grows.

value.command: for R in 6 8 10; do $G ensemble --soup 0.35 --radius $R --runs 16 --rng 1 --vary rule=B45/S3457 --gens 1000000; done

B45_S3457.src: research/NOTEBOOK.md 2026-11-12 "Rule space" with audit correction I5; CLAIMS Q3

B45_S3456.label: Survival at 6: a glass
B45_S3456.line: Allowing survival at six neighbours makes chaos slow down and lock into long cycles instead.

value.torus_32: activity decays 5% -> 0.2% of cells per gen over ~5000 gens at density 0.51; whole torus locks into cycles of period 120, 2280, 3312, 3960 (4 soups)

birth_at_3.label: Birth at three breaks the walls
birth_at_3.line: If faces can be born with three neighbours, chaos crosses diagonal planes and no box holds it.

strict_still_lifes_by_cells.label: Still lifes, counted exactly
strict_still_lifes_by_cells.line: Every motionless shape up to 16 faces has been counted; the count grows about fourfold per added face.

value.smallest: 6 cells, exactly 4 classes: S6a cube, KS6a kagome hexagon, S6b, S6c

law.label: Period = twist x loop
law.line: Long clocks are short loops that close only after their box turns or mirrors them; period is loop times twist.

value.statement: P = m * L, m = order of the box symmetry g with F^L(x) = g x; m in {1,2,3,4,6}; cells fixed by g have period dividing L

headline_objects.label: The long clocks
headline_objects.line: Each long period splits into a short loop and a small symmetry that closes it.

value.symmetry: S6 rotoreflection about (-1,1,1) (repo calls it a screw)
quarter turn about a cube axis (4-fold)

threshold_lemma.label: Only crowding keeps the clock running
threshold_lemma.line: Without overcrowded faces every closed system settles into stillness or blinking within 26 steps per face.

value.bound: period <= 2 within 26N + 1 steps (uncapped rule; for gump once no O1 events occur)
value.energy: E(t) = -x(t)^T (A+I) x(t-1) + 3.5(|x(t)| + |x(t-1)|), ordered pairs; Delta E = D - Q exactly; drive D >= 0 only at overcrowded cells (n >= 6) live at t-1, dissipation Q >= 0 elsewhere
value.consequence: every oscillator of period >= 3 has O1 events, at least R3/10 per period; finite vessels only
